title: Correlation Sidebar + Span Comparison Mode for Request Drilldowns
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Operators and SREs using Redwood Console need a fast way to compare two or more spans from distinct requests that share a correlation ID (example: model fallback path vs primary path). Current trace inspector prototypes show a single-pane waterfall; teams frequently asked for quick span-to-span comparison, cost-per-token context, and the ability to keep a focused correlation panel pinned while navigating other traces. This ticket proposes a correlation-focused sidebar plus a temporary 'Span Comparison Mode' that surfaces aligned timelines, side-by-side metadata and token-cost deltas for selected spans.
acceptance_criteria: Correlation Sidebar can be toggled from any trace drilldown and pins to the right side of the UI without losing scroll position in the main waterfall.
Span Comparison Mode supports selecting up to 3 spans (from same correlation ID across requests) and displays them in aligned mini-waterfalls for visual diffing.
Metadata comparison table shows attributes (service, host, GPU type, model variant, sequence length, tokens, cost estimate) with clear deltas and inline links to logs and request payloads.
Interactions: keyboard shortcut (C) to open sidebar, shift-click to multi-select spans, and Escape to exit compare mode.
Prototype reviewed by frontend lead and PM and usability-tested with 5 engineers; feedback items tracked and addressed.
Performance: sidebar virtualization strategy keeps initial render < 120ms for traces up to 5k spans.
Design spec contains redlines, focus states, color accessibility checks, and animation specs for timeline alignment.
Handoff artefacts: Figma file, interaction spec doc, and component tokens included in the handoff bundle.
design_notes: Sidebar is context-aware: when opened from a span it auto-selects related spans with same correlation ID and shows a compact histogram of request arrival times.
Span Comparison Mode aligns spans by request timestamp and displays a shared time ruler to surface skew and latency hotspots.
Introduce a lightweight cost estimator column that computes a normalized token-cost per-span using model and quantization metadata surfaced from the trace envelope.
Use a muted palette for non-selected spans and a high-contrast accent for active comparisons; ensure WCAG AA for 3:1 where possible.
Mobile behavior: sidebar collapses into a bottom-sheet with summary cards; full comparison reserved for desktop (secondary requirement).
Edge-case: for traces with >1000 spans we surface a summary view and require user to 'Zoom into segment' before enabling compare mode to avoid memory spikes.
We decided against full dual-canvas rendering (two independent waterfall canvases) because it doubled memory; instead we implement modular aligned mini-waterfalls per-span.
Include quick actions in each row: Open logs, Copy correlation ID, Open request in new tab, Pin pair for longer comparisons.
Suggested micro-interactions: gentle crossfade when adding/removing spans; nudge animation for new correlation matches discovered while sidebar is open.
Telemetry events to track: sidebar_opened, compare_mode_entered, span_selected_for_compare, compare_export_csv.
Accessibility: spans are keyboard-focusable; comparison table supports screen-reader summaries (short verbal diff).
decisions: Opted for a right-side collapsible sidebar instead of a modal to preserve trace context and enable persistent comparisons across navigations.
Limit compare selection to 3 spans to keep UI legible and to avoid overwhelming the metadata table.
Introduce an estimated 'cost delta' metric in the metadata table but label it as heuristic and link to billing details in the Console.
Virtualize long lists in the sidebar rather than paginate to keep interactions fluid for power users.
Keyboard shortcut chosen: 'C' for correlation sidebar to align with quick-context mental model; will validate in usability tests.
